title: Galois component presentation of a normal geometrically reduced variety
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $B$ be a nonempty normal integral proper finite-type $e$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] which is geometrically reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. There are a finite Galois extension $e_0/e$ [def-pc-field-extension] [def-pc-field-tower], its group $A=\operatorname{Aut}_e(e_0)$, and an open and closed integral component $X$ of $B_{e_0}=B\times_e e_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product] such that $X$ is normal, proper and geometrically integral over $e_0$. Here geometrically integral means integral after every extension of the base field. The scheme $B$ is Noetherian, meaning it has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The group $A$ permutes the components of $B_{e_0}$ transitively. Its stabilizer $H$ of $X$ acts faithfully on $X$ and on $e_0$, compatibly with $X\to\operatorname{Spec}e_0$. The restriction $u:X\to B$ is finite etale surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism], is $H$-invariant, and every geometric fibre of $u$ is a single $H$-orbit [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. If $C\subseteq B$ is the support of an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], then $u^{-1}C$ is the support of an $H$-stable effective Cartier divisor on $X$.

The orbit assertion concerns the finite etale component map, not an arbitrary alteration.

proof.text: For any field extension $F/e$, the scheme $B_F$ is of finite type over $F$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2). A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Its spectrum is quasi-compact, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] shows that $B_F$ is Noetherian. Taking $F=e$ proves the assertion for $B$, and this also supplies Noetherianity for each scalar extension used below.

Apply [lem-sbc-generic-components-split] to the finite-type morphism $B\to\operatorname{Spec}e$. It gives a finite field extension $L/e$, with etale spectrum map, for which every component of $B_L$ is geometrically irreducible. At the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}L$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable] says that $L/e$ is separable algebraic. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] with the one extension $L/e$: choose a finite Galois extension $e_0/e$ and an $e$-embedding $L\hookrightarrow e_0$. Regard this embedding as the intermediate field structure.

For $F=L,e_0$, write $p_F:B_F\to B$. The spectrum map of $F/e$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-ring-map-finite], etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale], and surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective]. Its base change $p_F$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] and is etale surjective by the singleton-cover case of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]. Step 1 gives $B_F$ Noetherian, while $B$ is normal integral by hypothesis. Thus [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] applies to $p_F$: both $B_L$ and $B_{e_0}$ are finite disjoint unions of nonempty clopen normal integral components. They are nonempty because $p_F$ is surjective and $B$ is nonempty.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150; component normality: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up); morphisms.tex Tags 01WL, 02GO

proof.text: For each clopen component $Z$ of $B_L$, take its inverse-image open subscheme $Z_{e_0}$ in $B_{e_0}$. For every extension $E/e_0$ its inverse image $Z_E$ is nonempty and irreducible by the geometric irreducibility supplied in step 2 (use the field tower $L\subseteq e_0\subseteq E$). Moreover $Z_E$ is open in $B_E$, which is reduced by the hypothesis on $B$ and [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Reducedness restricts to an open subscheme because its local rings are the same local rings. Hence $Z_E$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. In particular the $Z_{e_0}$ form a disjoint clopen irreducible covering, so they are precisely the components of $B_{e_0}$: an irreducible subset cannot meet both a clopen and its complement, and maximality then identifies each component. Thus every component is geometrically integral. Choose one and call it $X$. It is normal by step 3. The scheme $B_{e_0}$ is proper over $e_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]; its clopen subscheme $X$ is closed with the restricted scheme structure, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c) makes $X$ proper over $e_0$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, choice of the component Y_0; geometric integrality follows from geometric reducedness and the components split in Tag 054R

proof.text: Put $A=\operatorname{Aut}_e(e_0)$. Define its left action on $B_{e_0}$ by $a\mapsto\operatorname{id}_B\times\operatorname{Spec}(a^{-1})$; the inverse compensates for the contravariance of $\operatorname{Spec}$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the action law, $p_{e_0}a=p_{e_0}$, and compatibility with the same action on $\operatorname{Spec}e_0$. Each action map is an isomorphism, and therefore permutes irreducible components. Let $H=\{a\in A:aX=X\}$. Restricting the action to $H$ defines a semilinear action on $X$; the restriction $u=p_{e_0}|_X$ satisfies $uh=u$ for every $h\in H$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, Galois action and decomposition subgroup H

proof.text: Let $(X_i)$ be all the clopen components of $B_{e_0}$, including $X$, and put $u_i=p_{e_0}|_{X_i}$. Their inclusions form an etale covering by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Composing this covering with the singleton etale covering $p_{e_0}$ of step 3, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition] says that every $u_i$ is etale. The inclusions are also closed immersions, hence finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] makes every $u_i$ finite. Each $u_i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so its image is closed by the definition of properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its image is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] and nonempty since $X_i$ is nonempty. The integral space $B$ is irreducible, hence has no nonempty proper clopen subset. Consequently every $u_i$, and in particular $u$, is surjective.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, component restriction; Stacks morphisms.tex Tags 02GP, 035C, 01WK and 01WG

proof.text:
Fix any geometric point $\bar b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. By [def-weil-geometric-fibre] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the full fibre of $p_{e_0}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_e e_0)$. Choose an $e$-embedding $i:e_0\hookrightarrow\Omega$ using [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed]. The isomorphism in [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition](1), applied to $e_0/e$ and tensored along $i$ on the first factor, gives
$$\Omega\otimes_e e_0\simeq\prod_{a\in A}\Omega,\qquad c\otimes b\longmapsto(c\,i(a(b)))_a.$$
Here tensoring an isomorphism preserves its inverse; extension of scalars on a finite product is identified componentwise, with inverse obtained by summing the finitely many orthogonal coordinate idempotents. This verifies the displayed map directly. A prime of the finite product of fields selects exactly one coordinate: exactly one coordinate idempotent is outside the prime. The fibre is therefore a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, with geometric points indexed by the embeddings $i\circ a$. The action in step 5 permutes these indices by composition with automorphisms of $e_0$, hence simply transitively. This is a statement about geometric fibre points, including their residue-field embeddings.

source.place: Tag 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois), Galois-cover geometric fibres; explicit scalar-extension calculation from the tensor decomposition

proof.text: Each $u_i$ is surjective, so its base change to $\bar b$ is nonempty by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. It is the clopen part of the full fibre lying in $X_i$. By step 7 each such nonempty part contains a geometric point. For components $X_i,X_j$, choose points $x_i,x_j$ above the same $\bar b$. An element $a\in A$ takes $x_i$ to $x_j$ by step 7. Then $aX_i$ and $X_j$ meet at $x_j$; the components in step 3 are disjoint, so $aX_i=X_j$. Thus $A$ is transitive on components. For two points $x,y$ of the geometric fibre of $u$, step 7 gives $a\in A$ with $ax=y$. Now $aX$ meets $X$, so $aX=X$ and $a\in H$. The fibre is nonempty by surjectivity and consists of one $H$-orbit. Since $\bar b$ was arbitrary, this proves the assertion for every geometric fibre.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, transitivity on components and the contracted product; explicit stabilizer-fibre argument

proof.text: The action of $H$ on $e_0$ is faithful because $H$ is a subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}_e(e_0)$ (using inverses on the spectrum does not change its kernel). To check faithfulness on $X$, suppose $h\in H$ induces the identity of $X$. Choose a point $x\in X$, possible since $X$ is nonempty. On the residue field at $x$, semilinearity and the identity action imply $j(h^{-1}(c))=j(c)$ for all $c\in e_0$, where $j:e_0\to\kappa(x)$ is the structural field homomorphism. A unital homomorphism from a field into a field is injective, since its kernel is a proper ideal of the field. Thus $h^{-1}(c)=c$ for every $c$, and $h=1$. This proves faithfulness and retains the compatibility with the structure map established in step 5.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, application of 2.2 to the decomposition subgroup; explicit check of the faithful-action hypothesis

proof.text: Choose an effective Cartier divisor $D\subseteq B$ with support $C$. Since $u$ is etale it is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-pc-flat-pullback-effective-cartier-ideal] to obtain the effective Cartier divisor $D_X=D\times_B X$ on $X$. Locally if $D$ has equation $t$, then $D_X$ has equation $u^*t$, a nonzerodivisor, and its zero set is exactly $u^{-1}C$. For every $h\in H$, the equality $uh=u$ implies that pullback by $h$ preserves the ideal generated by these equations: $h^*(u^*\mathcal I_D)\mathcal O_X=u^*\mathcal I_D\mathcal O_X$. Consequently $D_X$ itself is $H$-stable, not only its support. This also includes the empty divisor.

The item is still unsplit in live and side-live. Its closure (519 nodes) has no node on either route-pivot-dropped list and no cycle; the only citer, lem-sfb-equivariant-smooth-galois-model, is not in it. Source: ILO X 2.3 Steps 1-2, printed p.150 (PDF p.156). The hypotheses match the Step-1 reductions and the conclusions are what Step 2 and the parent (steps 1 and 5) use. Step checks: (1) finite-type base change, and a finite-type scheme over Spec of a field is Noetherian. (2) 054R splitting L/e with étale spectrum, separable residue extension, Galois envelope with n=1. (3) p_F is finite, étale and surjective; lem-fin-etale-normal-components applies (W Noetherian, B normal integral). (4) For E ⊇ e0 ⊇ L each Z_E is irreducible and nonempty, and reduced as an open of reduced B_E, hence integral; the clopen pieces are the components; X proper by base change plus closed immersion. Minor: the step treats the clopen pieces of B_L as irreducible components without saying so; this is the same elementary clopen argument the step writes for B_{e0}, so no change. (5) I checked the left-action law of id×Spec(a⁻¹) and uh=u. (6) Each u_i is étale (covering composition) and finite, with closed and open nonempty image in irreducible B, hence surjective. (7) I checked that clause (1) of the tensor decomposition, base changed along i, gives c⊗b↦(c·i(a(b)))_a, and that the action is simply transitive on the |A| coordinate points. (8) This gives transitivity on components and one H-orbit in each geometric fibre of u. (9) Faithfulness on X from injectivity of e0→κ(x). (10) étale⇒flat; the 02OO flat pullback is Cartier, and h*(u*I)=u*I since uh=u. Edge cases checked: B already geometrically integral (A=1); B=Spec K with K/e separable (H=Gal(e0/K), fibres simply transitive); imperfect e; C empty. No duplicate presentation node in the DAG. I accept the five tool_uses (054R splitting, Galois envelope, 033C normal components, Galois tensor decomposition clause 1, 02OO flat Cartier pullback): all are generic and used through their statements only. No fixes.
